findings.body:
The change replaces `page * size` with `(page - 1) * size`, but `page` is a `usize` and the doc comment says pages are 0-based. For page 0, `page - 1` underflows: it panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds. The wrapped product then clamps to `items.len()`, so the function returns an empty slice instead of the first page.

Trigger: Calling `page(items, 0, size)` with any size, which is the documented first page.

Impact: Any caller that passes the documented 0-based first page gets a panic in debug builds or silently empty results in release builds. Search found no in-repo callers of `page(`, so the reachable impact is limited to external users of this public function.
findings.suggestion: Use `let start = page.saturating_mul(size).min(items.len());` to restore the 0-based contract, or change the doc and contract if 1-based pages are intended.
findings.title: page 0 underflows `page - 1` and returns an empty slice or panics

risk_level.reason: The diff changes the pagination offset to (page - 1) * size while the doc comment says page starts at 0, so page 0 underflows (panic in debug, wraps in release) and every page is shifted by one.
